summary.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready.” It is the standardized simplified counterpart of 備. One analysis of 備 depicts a person with an arrow container, suggesting readiness; another treats the graph as a picture of a quiver. The first graph’s role as a sound element is also proposed, but its historical sound relation is unresolved.

formation.text: 備 has competing analyses: one reads 人 as a person carrying 𤰈, an arrow container, and connects the scene with preparedness; the received analysis also assigns 𤰈 a phonetic role. Another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture. 备 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 備.

components.text: In one analysis of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the arrow container. Another interpretation treats the whole graph as a quiver picture, so the component breakdown is disputed.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, or a quiver. It is also assigned a phonetic role, though the pictured object’s original name and pronunciation are not independently recovered.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin readings of 𤰈 and 備 are both bèi, but this match does not establish their historical sound relation. The pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are not recovered.

sound.text: Both 𤰈 and 備 are listed with the modern Mandarin reading bèi. This current match does not establish that 𤰈 supplied 備’s historical sound.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but its earliest appearance and the sequence among these categories are unresolved.

The modern printed right-hand form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Some bronze forms also change 𤰈’s lower part to 用, tentatively treated as a sound element; these descriptions do not establish a dated sequence.
In 1956, 备 was standardized as the simplified counterpart of 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but its specific role in the formation of 备 is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the graph’s association with readiness, but it does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 備 is also reported as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” in a bronze inscription. This may be sound-based borrowing, but the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are unrecovered, so the sound match is unverified.

Reported meanings include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these senses.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may help explain preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; this does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.

overview.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready” and is the simplified counterpart of 備. One analysis of 備 pictures a person carrying an arrow container, suggesting readiness; another treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.

components.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the container.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container; whether it also supplied a sound cue remains disputed.

relationships.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person in a carrying scene.
𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container in the proposed carrying scene; another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.
A received analysis assigns 𤰈 a sound role in 備. Modern Mandarin lists both 𤰈 and 備 as bèi, but no independent historical pronunciation for 𤰈 was recovered to establish the relation.
The 1956 scheme lists 备 as the simplified form corresponding to 備.
俻 is documented as a variant of 備; this does not establish that 备 specifically derives from 俻.
